applies_why: This judge text does not count a cited-in verse as an unanswered witness or toward a broken link; it treats the Acts 2:30 row as underdetermined and notes that the verses were answered.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: unanswered witness / broken link: I weighed applying K-G4 to any discussion of a cited-in verse versus applying it only when a verse is counted as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; this text treats the row as underdetermined, not as a broken link.
why: Because the judge text says the verses were answered and reaches underdetermined rather than counting any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link, it does not violate K-G4.
